title: Mental Foramen Bypass for Prosthetically Favorable Implant Positioning in the Atrophied Mandible
content:
Background/Objectives: Severe posterior mandibular atrophy is often limiting for implant placement due to diminished bone height and proximity to the mental fora-men with its anatomical variations, particularly the anterior loop. Conventional solutions may require invasive procedures or result in prosthetic cantilevers. Utilization of available lingual bone to bypass the mental foramen may represent a less invasive alternative; however, anatomical evidence supporting this concept remains limited. The aim of this retrospective study was to evaluate the availability of lingual bone adjacent to the mental foramen in atrophied mandibles using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), thereby determining the feasibility of a mental foramen bypass approach for implant placement. 
Methods: 110 CBCT scans of adult patients with atrophied mandibles were analyzed. Linear measurements were obtained from the lingual cortical plate to the mesial (Point A), middle (Point B), and distal (Point C) borders of the mental foramen. The presence of the anterior loop was recorded. Descriptive statistics and independent-samples t-tests were performed to compare measurements between loop and no-loop groups (α = 0.05). 
Results: The mean measurements of the lingual bone were 7.22 ± 1.65 mm at Point A, 6.18 ± 1.55 mm at Point B, and 4.82 ± 1.38 mm at Point C, showing a gradual decrease from mesial to distal. An anterior loop was found in 26.4% of the cases. Significantly thinner dimensions of the lingual bone were observed with an anterior loop at all three measurement points (P <  .01). Implant placement lingual to the mental foramen in the clinical case was possible without neurosensory complications. 
Conclusions: These observations provide a good back-ground from an anatomical point of view to mental foramen bypass concept as a less invasive alternative to the nerve repositioning procedures, creating the possibility for more distally positioned implant placement, reducing prosthetic cantilever length, and enhancing prosthetically favorable implant-supported rehabilitation in atrophied mandibles.
